Orange is a legend and this chain is extremely impressive here.

No memory corruptions, no heap shenanigans, just pure logic bugs, almost made easy to understand for the reader.

As a bonus, they also posted a reverse chain: popping Edge from calc [0].

[0] https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bh1zglq4mLE

I always felt bad about the whole site/browser cross integration that chrome and edge and others do. Now I feel really really really bad about it. Can almost see the marketing team's emails about what features to add, and the developers unwantingly writing the code not expecting such things to open so many holes

Oh dear god, at each further chain link I was laughing so hard that my poor cats got disturbed!

This entire chain is nothing but a lesson of shame for Microsoft - if you fork a thing, better be prepared to thoroughly understand and review each corner you touch. Or you might miss important cross-references that you should update but that aren't mentioned in comments by the original developers.

As for the "sign in automatically" BS that both Google and Edge push - that can go and die in a hellfire where it belongs.
It's very refreshing to read such clearly written and concise technical reports.

> with a simple fetch(...) with credentials included, you can easily grab any Microsoft Edge user’s email from any website

Wow, this is disturbing on its own

> So even if you’ve never created a User Profile in the browser, just visiting www.microsoft.com is enough for Edge to create one and sign you in automatically.

This is disgusting behaviour, RCE chain or not.

I guess that explains the questions I had when I was mysteriously logged into Edge. I checked whether Chrome does something similar, and it can, but the setting "Sign in to Chrome when you sign in to other Google services" was set to "Don't sign in", so I'm not sure whether this is the default or not.
human craft is becoming rare these days

Glad to now have some hard evidence I can reference whenever I bring up my strongly held intuitive opinion of "Microsoft repackaging someone else's browser  and adding some extra stuff to it can only make Edge strictly worse"
This is very awesome and cool.

A good summary of the so-called "modern" browser

But what hapens when there's no Javascript interpreter, i.e., not the so-called "modern" browser

And when the OS is not Windows

The so-called "modern" browser _is_ a "logic bug". It's multiple layers of stupidity if "security" is a goal
